question: The oldest and most continuously productive coalfield in India, located in West Bengal, is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raniganj Coalfield**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Raniganj Coalfield** is the oldest coalfield in India, where mining activities first commenced in **1774** during the tenure of the British East India Company.
 
• It was discovered by **John Sumner** and **Suetonius Grant Heatly**, who identified coal seams along the **Damodar River**.
 
• Geographically, it is primarily situated in the **Paschim Bardhaman** district of **West Bengal**, extending partially into the **Dhanbad** district of **Jharkhand**.
 
• The coalfield belongs to the **Gondwana period** and is characterized by its high-quality **non-coking coal**, which features low ash content and high volatile matter.
 
• It remains one of the most productive regions under the administration of **Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL)**, a subsidiary of **Coal India Limited**.
 
• The region is a critical supplier for **Thermal Power Plants** and industries across **Eastern India**, maintaining production continuity for over two centuries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jharia Coalfield**

 
 
• Located in **Jharkhand**, it is the largest coalfield in India and the primary source of high-grade **coking coal** used in **blast furnaces**.
 
• It is notorious for long-standing **underground coal fires** that have persisted for decades.
 
 
 
• **Bokaro Coalfield**
 
 
• Situated in the **Bokaro district** of **Jharkhand**, it is divided into East and West sections.
 
• It supplies essential fuel to the **Bokaro Steel Plant** and various **metallurgical** industries.
 
 
 
• **Talcher Coalfield**
 
 
• Located in the **Angul district** of **Odisha** within the **Brahmani River** valley.
 
• It holds the largest **geological reserves** of coal in India, managed by **Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL)**.
